"""
Example 1: Named Entity Recognition with CRF
"""
def example_ner_with_crf():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Example: Named Entity Recognition with CRF")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    # Simulate NER task
    batch_size = 2
    seq_len = 15
    vocab_size = 1000
    embedding_dim = 128
    hidden_dim = 256
    num_tags = 9  # B-PER, I-PER, B-LOC, I-LOC, B-ORG, I-ORG, B-MISC, I-MISC, O
    
    class NERModel(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
            super().__init__()
            self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embedding_dim)
            self.lstm = nn.LSTM(
                embedding_dim,
                hidden_dim // 2,
                num_layers=2,
                bidirectional=True,
                batch_first=True,
                dropout=0.3
            )
            self.dropout = nn.Dropout(0.5)
            self.hidden2tag = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, num_tags)
            self.crf = CRFLayer(num_tags)
        
        def forward(self, sentences, tags=None, mask=None):
            # sentences: [batch, seq_len]
            # tags: [batch, seq_len] (optional, for training)
            # mask: [batch, seq_len] (optional)
            
            # Embedding
            embeds = self.embedding(sentences)  # [batch, seq_len, emb_dim]
            
            # LSTM
            lstm_out, _ = self.lstm(embeds)  # [batch, seq_len, hidden_dim]
            lstm_out = self.dropout(lstm_out)
            
            # Emission scores
            emissions = self.hidden2tag(lstm_out)  # [batch, seq_len, num_tags]
            
            if tags is not None:
                # Training: return negative log-likelihood
                return self.crf(emissions, tags, mask)
            else:
                # Inference: return emissions for decoding
                return emissions
        
        def decode(self, sentences, mask=None):
            emissions = self.forward(sentences, tags=None, mask=mask)
            return self.crf.decode(emissions, mask)
    
    # Create model
    model = NERModel()
    
    # Sample data
    sentences = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (batch_size, seq_len))
    tags = torch.randint(0, num_tags, (batch_size, seq_len))
    
    # Mask (first sequence is full, second is shorter)
    mask = torch.ones(batch_size, seq_len)
    mask[1, 12:] = 0
    
    print(f"Input sentences shape: {sentences.shape}")
    print(f"Tags shape: {tags.shape}")
    
    # Training step
    model.train()
    loss = model(sentences, tags, mask)
    print(f"\nTraining loss: {loss.item():.4f}")
    
    # Inference
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        predictions = model.decode(sentences, mask)
    
    print(f"\nPredicted tags for first sequence: {predictions[0]}")
    print(f"True tags for first sequence: {tags[0].tolist()}")
    print(f"Predicted tags for second sequence: {predictions[1]}")
    print(f"True tags for second sequence: {tags[1, :12].tolist()}")
    
    print("\n")


"""
Example 2: Image Segmentation with MRF
"""
def example_segmentation_with_mrf():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Example: Image Segmentation with MRF")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    batch_size = 2
    num_classes = 21  # PASCAL VOC classes
    height, width = 64, 64
    in_channels = 3
    
    class SegmentationModel(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
            super().__init__()
            # Feature extractor (simple CNN)
            self.encoder = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, 64, 3, padding=1),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.MaxPool2d(2),
                nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.MaxPool2d(2),
                nn.Conv2d(128, 256, 3, padding=1),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(256),
                nn.ReLU(),
            )
            
            # Upsample
            self.upsample = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2, mode='bilinear', align_corners=True),
                nn.Conv2d(256, 128, 3, padding=1),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2, mode='bilinear', align_corners=True),
                nn.Conv2d(128, 64, 3, padding=1),
                nn.ReLU(),
            )
            
            # MRF for structured output
            self.mrf = MarkovRandomField(
                num_classes=num_classes,
                spatial_dims=(height, width),
                unary_features=64,
                use_pairwise=True,
                neighborhood_size=1
            )
        
        def forward(self, images, num_mrf_iterations=5):
            # Encode
            features = self.encoder(images)
            features = self.upsample(features)
            
            # Apply MRF
            unary_pred, refined_pred = self.mrf(features, num_mrf_iterations)
            
            return unary_pred, refined_pred
    
    # Create model
    model = SegmentationModel()
    
    # Sample data
    images = torch.randn(batch_size, in_channels, height, width)
    masks = torch.randint(0, num_classes, (batch_size, height, width))
    
    print(f"Input images shape: {images.shape}")
    print(f"Ground truth masks shape: {masks.shape}")
    
    # Forward pass
    unary_pred, refined_pred = model(images, num_mrf_iterations=5)
    
    print(f"\nUnary predictions shape: {unary_pred.shape}")
    print(f"Refined predictions shape: {refined_pred.shape}")
    
    # Compute losses
    loss_unary = F.cross_entropy(unary_pred, masks)
    loss_refined = F.cross_entropy(refined_pred, masks)
    
    print(f"\nUnary loss: {loss_unary.item():.4f}")
    print(f"Refined loss (with MRF): {loss_refined.item():.4f}")
    print(f"Improvement: {(loss_unary - loss_refined).item():.4f}")
    
    # Decode predictions
    pred_masks = torch.argmax(refined_pred, dim=1)
    accuracy = (pred_masks == masks).float().mean()
    print(f"Pixel accuracy: {accuracy.item():.2%}")
    
    print("\n")


"""
Example 3: Molecular Property Prediction with Graph Models
"""
def example_molecular_prediction():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Example: Molecular Property Prediction")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    # Simulate molecular graph
    num_atoms = 20
    atom_features = 16
    bond_features = 4
    num_atom_types = 5
    
    class MolecularModel(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
            super().__init__()
            self.atom_embedding = nn.Embedding(num_atom_types, atom_features)
            
            self.gnn = GraphicalModelLayer(
                node_features=atom_features,
                edge_features=bond_features,
                hidden_dim=64,
                num_classes=num_atom_types,
                num_message_passing=4
            )
            
            # Global pooling and prediction
            self.global_pool = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(64, 32),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Linear(32, 1)  # Property prediction (e.g., solubility)
            )
        
        def forward(self, atom_types, edge_index, edge_features):
            # Embed atoms
            node_features = self.atom_embedding(atom_types)
            
            # Apply GNN
            node_scores, edge_scores = self.gnn(
                node_features,
                edge_index,
                edge_features
            )
            
            # Global pooling (mean over nodes)
            graph_features = node_scores.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
            
            # Predict property
            property_pred = self.global_pool(graph_features)
            
            return property_pred, node_scores, edge_scores
    
    # Create model
    model = MolecularModel()
    
    # Sample molecular graph
    atom_types = torch.randint(0, num_atom_types, (num_atoms,))
    
    # Create bonds (edges)
    edge_list = []
    for i in range(num_atoms - 1):
        edge_list.append([i, i + 1])
        edge_list.append([i + 1, i])
    # Add some additional bonds
    edge_list.extend([[0, 5], [5, 0], [3, 8], [8, 3]])
    edge_index = torch.tensor(edge_list).t()
    
    num_bonds = edge_index.shape[1]
    edge_features = torch.randn(num_bonds, bond_features)
    
    print(f"Number of atoms: {num_atoms}")
    print(f"Number of bonds: {num_bonds}")
    print(f"Atom types: {atom_types.tolist()}")
    
    # Forward pass
    property_pred, node_scores, edge_scores = model(
        atom_types,
        edge_index,
        edge_features
    )
    
    print(f"\nPredicted property: {property_pred.item():.4f}")
    print(f"Node scores shape: {node_scores.shape}")
    print(f"Edge scores shape: {edge_scores.shape}")
    
    # Decode node predictions
    node_predictions = torch.argmax(node_scores, dim=1)
    print(f"Node predictions: {node_predictions.tolist()}")
    
    print("\n")


"""
Example 4: Video Action Segmentation with Energy-Based Model
"""
def example_video_action_segmentation():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Example: Video Action Segmentation")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    batch_size = 1
    num_frames = 30
    frame_features = 512
    action_dim = 10
    num_actions = 5
    
    class VideoSegmentationModel(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
            super().__init__()
            # Frame encoder
            self.frame_encoder = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(frame_features, 256),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.3),
                nn.Linear(256, 128)
            )
            
            # Energy-based structured output
            self.ebm = EnergyBasedStructuredOutput(
                input_dim=128,
                output_dim=action_dim,
                hidden_dims=[256, 128, 64],
                structure_type='sequence',
                use_contrastive=True
            )
            
            # Action classifier
            self.action_classifier = nn.Linear(action_dim, num_actions)
        
        def forward(self, frame_features, action_sequences=None):
            # Encode frames
            batch_size, num_frames, _ = frame_features.shape
            encoded = self.frame_encoder(
                frame_features.reshape(-1, frame_features.shape[-1])
            )
            encoded = encoded.reshape(batch_size, num_frames, -1)
            
            # Pool to get video-level representation
            video_repr = encoded.mean(dim=1)
            
            if action_sequences is not None:
                # Training: compute energy
                energy = self.ebm(video_repr, action_sequences)
                return energy
            else:
                # Inference: generate action sequence
                return None
        
        def generate_actions(self, frame_features, num_iterations=50):
            # Encode frames
            batch_size, num_frames, _ = frame_features.shape
            encoded = self.frame_encoder(
                frame_features.reshape(-1, frame_features.shape[-1])
            )
            encoded = encoded.reshape(batch_size, num_frames, -1)
            video_repr = encoded.mean(dim=1)
            
            # Generate action sequence
            action_seq = self.ebm.generate(
                video_repr,
                output_shape=(num_frames,),
                num_iterations=num_iterations,
                learning_rate=0.05
            )
            
            # Classify actions
            action_logits = self.action_classifier(
                action_seq.reshape(-1, action_dim)
            )
            action_labels = torch.argmax(action_logits, dim=-1)
            action_labels = action_labels.reshape(batch_size, num_frames)
            
            return action_labels, action_seq
    
    # Create model
    model = VideoSegmentationModel()
    
    # Sample video data
    video_features = torch.randn(batch_size, num_frames, frame_features)
    
    print(f"Video features shape: {video_features.shape}")
    
    # Generate action sequence
    print("\nGenerating action sequence...")
    action_labels, action_seq = model.generate_actions(
        video_features,
        num_iterations=30
    )
    
    print(f"Generated action labels: {action_labels[0].tolist()}")
    print(f"Action sequence shape: {action_seq.shape}")
    
    # Count action transitions
    transitions = 0
    for i in range(num_frames - 1):
        if action_labels[0, i] != action_labels[0, i + 1]:
            transitions += 1
    print(f"Number of action transitions: {transitions}")
    
    print("\n")


"""
Example 5: Complete Training Loop for Sequence Labeling
"""
def example_complete_training():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Example: Complete Training Loop")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    # Hyperparameters
    vocab_size = 5000
    embedding_dim = 100
    hidden_dim
```python
    # Hyperparameters
    vocab_size = 5000
    embedding_dim = 100
    hidden_dim = 128
    num_tags = 7
    num_epochs = 5
    batch_size = 16
    learning_rate = 0.001
    
    # Create synthetic dataset
    class SyntheticSequenceDataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
        def __init__(self, num_samples, seq_len_range=(5, 20)):
            self.num_samples = num_samples
            self.seq_len_range = seq_len_range
            
            # Generate data
            self.data = []
            for _ in range(num_samples):
                seq_len = torch.randint(seq_len_range[0], seq_len_range[1] + 1, (1,)).item()
                tokens = torch.randint(1, vocab_size, (seq_len,))
                # Generate tags with some structure (consecutive tags tend to be similar)
                tags = torch.zeros(seq_len, dtype=torch.long)
                tags[0] = torch.randint(0, num_tags, (1,)).item()
                for i in range(1, seq_len):
                    # 70% chance to keep same tag, 30% to change
                    if torch.rand(1).item() < 0.7:
                        tags[i] = tags[i-1]
                    else:
                        tags[i] = torch.randint(0, num_tags, (1,)).item()
                
                self.data.append((tokens, tags))
        
        def __len__(self):
            return self.num_samples
        
        def __getitem__(self, idx):
            return self.data[idx]
    
    # Collate function for variable-length sequences
    def collate_fn(batch):
        tokens_list, tags_list = zip(*batch)
        
        # Get max length
        max_len = max(len(t) for t in tokens_list)
        
        # Pad sequences
        tokens_padded = torch.zeros(len(batch), max_len, dtype=torch.long)
        tags_padded = torch.zeros(len(batch), max_len, dtype=torch.long)
        mask = torch.zeros(len(batch), max_len, dtype=torch.float)
        
        for i, (tokens, tags) in enumerate(zip(tokens_list, tags_list)):
            seq_len = len(tokens)
            tokens_padded[i, :seq_len] = tokens
            tags_padded[i, :seq_len] = tags
            mask[i, :seq_len] = 1.0
        
        return tokens_padded, tags_padded, mask
    
    # Create model
    class SequenceLabelingModel(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, vocab_size, embedding_dim, hidden_dim, num_tags):
            super().__init__()
            self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embedding_dim, padding_idx=0)
            self.dropout = nn.Dropout(0.3)
            
            self.lstm = nn.LSTM(
                embedding_dim,
                hidden_dim // 2,
                num_layers=2,
                bidirectional=True,
                batch_first=True,
                dropout=0.3
            )
            
            self.hidden2tag = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, num_tags)
            self.crf = CRFLayer(num_tags, include_start_end_transitions=True)
        
        def forward(self, tokens, tags=None, mask=None):
            # Embedding
            embeds = self.embedding(tokens)
            embeds = self.dropout(embeds)
            
            # LSTM
            lstm_out, _ = self.lstm(embeds)
            lstm_out = self.dropout(lstm_out)
            
            # Emissions
            emissions = self.hidden2tag(lstm_out)
            
            if tags is not None:
                # Training: compute CRF loss
                loss = self.crf(emissions, tags, mask, reduction='mean')
                return loss
            else:
                # Inference: decode
                return emissions
        
        def decode(self, tokens, mask=None):
            emissions = self.forward(tokens, tags=None, mask=mask)
            return self.crf.decode(emissions, mask)
    
    # Create datasets and loaders
    print("Creating datasets...")
    train_dataset = SyntheticSequenceDataset(num_samples=1000)
    val_dataset = SyntheticSequenceDataset(num_samples=200)
    
    train_loader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(
        train_dataset,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        shuffle=True,
        collate_fn=collate_fn
    )
    
    val_loader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(
        val_dataset,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        shuffle=False,
        collate_fn=collate_fn
    )
    
    # Create model and optimizer
    print("Initializing model...")
    model = SequenceLabelingModel(vocab_size, embedding_dim, hidden_dim, num_tags)
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
    scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(
        optimizer, mode='min', factor=0.5, patience=2, verbose=True
    )
    
    # Training loop
    print("\nStarting training...")
    print("-" * 60)
    
    best_val_loss = float('inf')
    
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        # Training
        model.train()
        train_loss = 0.0
        train_batches = 0
        
        for tokens, tags, mask in train_loader:
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            
            # Forward pass
            loss = model(tokens, tags, mask)
            
            # Backward pass
            loss.backward()
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 5.0)
            optimizer.step()
            
            train_loss += loss.item()
            train_batches += 1
        
        avg_train_loss = train_loss / train_batches
        
        # Validation
        model.eval()
        val_loss = 0.0
        val_batches = 0
        correct_tags = 0
        total_tags = 0
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for tokens, tags, mask in val_loader:
                # Compute loss
                loss = model(tokens, tags, mask)
                val_loss += loss.item()
                val_batches += 1
                
                # Compute accuracy
                predictions = model.decode(tokens, mask)
                for pred, true_tags, m in zip(predictions, tags, mask):
                    seq_len = int(m.sum().item())
                    pred_tensor = torch.tensor(pred[:seq_len])
                    true_tensor = true_tags[:seq_len]
                    correct_tags += (pred_tensor == true_tensor).sum().item()
                    total_tags += seq_len
        
        avg_val_loss = val_loss / val_batches
        accuracy = correct_tags / total_tags if total_tags > 0 else 0.0
        
        # Update learning rate
        scheduler.step(avg_val_loss)
        
        # Print progress
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{num_epochs}")
        print(f"  Train Loss: {avg_train_loss:.4f}")
        print(f"  Val Loss: {avg_val_loss:.4f}")
        print(f"  Val Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f} ({accuracy*100:.2f}%)")
        
        # Save best model
        if avg_val_loss < best_val_loss:
            best_val_loss = avg_val_loss
            print(f"  New best model! (Val Loss: {best_val_loss:.4f})")
    
    print("\nTraining completed!")
    print(f"Best validation loss: {best_val_loss:.4f}")
    
    # Test inference on a sample
    print("\n" + "-" * 60)
    print("Sample Inference:")
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        sample_tokens, sample_tags, sample_mask = next(iter(val_loader))
        predictions = model.decode(sample_tokens[:1], sample_mask[:1])
        
        seq_len = int(sample_mask[0].sum().item())
        print(f"Input tokens: {sample_tokens[0, :seq_len].tolist()}")
        print(f"Predicted tags: {predictions[0]}")
        print(f"True tags: {sample_tags[0, :seq_len].tolist()}")
        
        # Compute sample accuracy
        pred_tensor = torch.tensor(predictions[0])
        true_tensor = sample_tags[0, :seq_len]
        sample_acc = (pred_tensor == true_tensor).float().mean().item()
        print(f"Sample accuracy: {sample_acc:.4f} ({sample_acc*100:.2f}%)")
    
    print("\n")


"""
Example 6: Multi-task Structured Output
"""
def example_multitask_structured_output():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Example: Multi-task Structured Output")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    batch_size = 4
    seq_len = 12
    input_dim = 64
    num_pos_tags = 10  # Part-of-speech tags
    num_ner_tags = 7   # Named entity tags
    
    class MultiTaskModel(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
            super().__init__()
            # Shared encoder
            self.shared_encoder = nn.LSTM(
                input_dim,
                128,
                num_layers=2,
                bidirectional=True,
                batch_first=True,
                dropout=0.3
            )
            
            # Task-specific layers
            self.pos_projection = nn.Linear(256, num_pos_tags)
            self.ner_projection = nn.Linear(256, num_ner_tags)
            
            # Task-specific CRFs
            self.pos_crf = CRFLayer(num_pos_tags)
            self.ner_crf = CRFLayer(num_ner_tags)
        
        def forward(self, x, pos_tags=None, ner_tags=None, mask=None):
            # Shared encoding
            shared_features, _ = self.shared_encoder(x)
            
            # POS tagging
            pos_emissions = self.pos_projection(shared_features)
            if pos_tags is not None:
                pos_loss = self.pos_crf(pos_emissions, pos_tags, mask)
            else:
                pos_loss = None
            
            # NER tagging
            ner_emissions = self.ner_projection(shared_features)
            if ner_tags is not None:
                ner_loss = self.ner_crf(ner_emissions, ner_tags, mask)
            else:
                ner_loss = None
            
            if pos_loss is not None and ner_loss is not None:
                # Multi-task loss (weighted sum)
                total_loss = 0.5 * pos_loss + 0.5 * ner_loss
                return total_loss, pos_loss, ner_loss
            else:
                return pos_emissions, ner_emissions
        
        def decode(self, x, mask=None):
            pos_emissions, ner_emissions = self.forward(x, mask=mask)
            pos_predictions = self.pos_crf.decode(pos_emissions, mask)
            ner_predictions = self.ner_crf.decode(ner_emissions, mask)
            return pos_predictions, ner_predictions
    
    # Create model
    model = MultiTaskModel()
    
    # Sample data
    x = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, input_dim)
    pos_tags = torch.randint(0, num_pos_tags, (batch_size, seq_len))
    ner_tags = torch.randint(0, num_ner_tags, (batch_size, seq_len))
    mask = torch.ones(batch_size, seq_len)
    mask[:, -2:] = 0  # Variable length sequences
    
    print(f"Input shape: {x.shape}")
    print(f"POS tags shape: {pos_tags.shape}")
    print(f"NER tags shape: {ner_tags.shape}")
    
    # Training
    model.train()
    total_loss, pos_loss, ner_loss = model(x, pos_tags, ner_tags, mask)
    
    print(f"\nTraining losses:")
    print(f"  Total loss: {total_loss.item():.4f}")
    print(f"  POS loss: {pos_loss.item():.4f}")
    print(f"  NER loss: {ner_loss.item():.4f}")
    
    # Inference
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        pos_preds, ner_preds = model.decode(x, mask)
    
    print(f"\nPredictions:")
    print(f"  POS predictions (first seq): {pos_preds[0]}")
    print(f"  NER predictions (first seq): {ner_preds[0]}")
    print(f"  True POS tags (first seq): {pos_tags[0, :len(pos_preds[0])].tolist()}")
    print(f"  True NER tags (first seq): {ner_tags[0, :len(ner_preds[0])].tolist()}")
    
    print("\n")


"""
Performance Comparison Utility
"""
def compare_structured_methods():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Performance Comparison: Structured vs Unstructured")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    batch_size = 8
    seq_len = 15
    input_dim = 32
    num_classes = 5
    
    # Unstructured model (simple classification)
    class UnstructuredModel(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
            super().__init__()
            self.lstm = nn.LSTM(input_dim, 64, batch_first=True)
            self.classifier = nn.Linear(64, num_classes)
        
        def forward(self, x):
            lstm_out, _ = self.lstm(x)
            logits = self.classifier(lstm_out)
            return logits
    
    # Structured model (with CRF)
    class StructuredModel(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
            super().__init__()
            self.lstm = nn.LSTM(input_dim, 64, batch_first=True)
            self.hidden2tag = nn.Linear(64, num_classes)
            self.crf = CRFLayer(num_classes)
        
        def forward(self, x, tags=None, mask=None):
            lstm_out, _ = self.lstm(x)
            emissions = self.hidden2tag(lstm_out)
            
            if tags is not None:
                return self.crf(emissions, tags, mask)
            return emissions
        
        def decode(self, x, mask=None):
            emissions = self.forward(x)
            return self.crf.decode(emissions, mask)
    
    # Create models
    unstructured = UnstructuredModel()
    structured = StructuredModel()
    
    # Generate synthetic data with structure
    # (consecutive labels tend to be the same)
    x = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, input_dim)
    
```python
    # Generate synthetic data with structure
    # (consecutive labels tend to be the same)
    x = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, input_dim)
    tags = torch.zeros(batch_size, seq_len, dtype=torch.long)
    for b in range(batch_size):
        tags[b, 0] = torch.randint(0, num_classes, (1,)).item()
        for t in range(1, seq_len):
            # 80% chance to keep same tag (strong structure)
            if torch.rand(1).item() < 0.8:
                tags[b, t] = tags[b, t-1]
            else:
                tags[b, t] = torch.randint(0, num_classes, (1,)).item()
    
    mask = torch.ones(batch_size, seq_len)
    
    print("Testing on data with strong sequential structure...")
    print(f"Sample sequence: {tags[0].tolist()}")
    
    # Test unstructured model
    unstructured.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = unstructured(x)
        unstruct_preds = torch.argmax(logits, dim=-1)
    
    unstruct_acc = (unstruct_preds == tags).float().mean().item()
    
    # Count transitions in unstructured predictions
    unstruct_transitions = 0
    for b in range(batch_size):
        for t in range(seq_len - 1):
            if unstruct_preds[b, t] != unstruct_preds[b, t+1]:
                unstruct_transitions += 1
    unstruct_transitions /= (batch_size * (seq_len - 1))
    
    # Test structured model
    structured.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        struct_preds_list = structured.decode(x, mask)
        struct_preds = torch.zeros_like(tags)
        for b in range(batch_size):
            struct_preds[b] = torch.tensor(struct_preds_list[b])
    
    struct_acc = (struct_preds == tags).float().mean().item()
    
    # Count transitions in structured predictions
    struct_transitions = 0
    for b in range(batch_size):
        for t in range(seq_len - 1):
            if struct_preds[b, t] != struct_preds[b, t+1]:
                struct_transitions += 1
    struct_transitions /= (batch_size * (seq_len - 1))
    
    # Ground truth transitions
    true_transitions = 0
    for b in range(batch_size):
        for t in range(seq_len - 1):
            if tags[b, t] != tags[b, t+1]:
                true_transitions += 1
    true_transitions /= (batch_size * (seq_len - 1))
    
    print(f"\nResults:")
    print(f"  Unstructured Model:")
    print(f"    Accuracy: {unstruct_acc:.4f} ({unstruct_acc*100:.2f}%)")
    print(f"    Transition rate: {unstruct_transitions:.4f}")
    print(f"\n  Structured Model (CRF):")
    print(f"    Accuracy: {struct_acc:.4f} ({struct_acc*100:.2f}%)")
    print(f"    Transition rate: {struct_transitions:.4f}")
    print(f"\n  Ground Truth:")
    print(f"    Transition rate: {true_transitions:.4f}")
    
    print(f"\nImprovement: {(struct_acc - unstruct_acc)*100:.2f}% absolute")
    print(f"Transition rate match (structured): {abs(struct_transitions - true_transitions):.4f}")
    print(f"Transition rate match (unstructured): {abs(unstruct_transitions - true_transitions):.4f}")
    
    print("\n")


"""
Hyperparameter Tuning Example
"""
def example_hyperparameter_tuning():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Example: Hyperparameter Tuning for Structured Models")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    batch_size = 16
    seq_len = 10
    input_dim = 32
    num_tags = 5
    num_samples = 200
    
    # Create simple dataset
    class SimpleDataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
        def __init__(self, num_samples):
            self.x = torch.randn(num_samples, seq_len, input_dim)
            self.y = torch.randint(0, num_tags, (num_samples, seq_len))
        
        def __len__(self):
            return len(self.x)
        
        def __getitem__(self, idx):
            return self.x[idx], self.y[idx]
    
    dataset = SimpleDataset(num_samples)
    loader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)
    
    # Hyperparameter configurations
    configs = [
        {'hidden_dim': 64, 'num_layers': 1, 'lr': 0.01, 'name': 'Config 1'},
        {'hidden_dim': 128, 'num_layers': 2, 'lr': 0.001, 'name': 'Config 2'},
        {'hidden_dim': 256, 'num_layers': 2, 'lr': 0.0001, 'name': 'Config 3'},
    ]
    
    results = []
    
    for config in configs:
        print(f"\nTesting {config['name']}:")
        print(f"  Hidden dim: {config['hidden_dim']}")
        print(f"  Num layers: {config['num_layers']}")
        print(f"  Learning rate: {config['lr']}")
        
        # Create model
        class ConfigModel(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self, hidden_dim, num_layers):
                super().__init__()
                self.lstm = nn.LSTM(
                    input_dim, hidden_dim,
                    num_layers=num_layers,
                    batch_first=True
                )
                self.hidden2tag = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, num_tags)
                self.crf = CRFLayer(num_tags)
            
            def forward(self, x, tags=None):
                lstm_out, _ = self.lstm(x)
                emissions = self.hidden2tag(lstm_out)
                if tags is not None:
                    return self.crf(emissions, tags)
                return emissions
        
        model = ConfigModel(config['hidden_dim'], config['num_layers'])
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=config['lr'])
        
        # Quick training (3 epochs)
        model.train()
        total_loss = 0
        num_batches = 0
        
        for epoch in range(3):
            for x, y in loader:
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                loss = model(x, y)
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                total_loss += loss.item()
                num_batches += 1
        
        avg_loss = total_loss / num_batches
        
        # Count parameters
        num_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
        
        results.append({
            'config': config['name'],
            'loss': avg_loss,
            'params': num_params
        })
        
        print(f"  Avg Loss: {avg_loss:.4f}")
        print(f"  Num Parameters: {num_params:,}")
    
    # Print summary
    print("\n" + "-" * 60)
    print("Summary:")
    print("-" * 60)
    for result in results:
        print(f"{result['config']}: Loss={result['loss']:.4f}, Params={result['params']:,}")
    
    best_config = min(results, key=lambda x: x['loss'])
    print(f"\nBest configuration: {best_config['config']} (Loss: {best_config['loss']:.4f})")
    
    print("\n")


"""
Debugging and Visualization Tools
"""
class StructuredOutputDebugger:
    """
    Utility class for debugging structured output models.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def visualize_crf_transitions(crf_layer, class_names=None):
        """Visualize CRF transition matrix."""
        print("=" * 60)
        print("CRF Transition Matrix Visualization")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        transitions = crf_layer.transitions.detach().cpu().numpy()
        num_tags = transitions.shape[0]
        
        if class_names is None:
            class_names = [f"Tag_{i}" for i in range(num_tags)]
        
        print("\nTransition scores (from row to column):")
        print("Higher scores indicate more likely transitions\n")
        
        # Print header
        header = "        " + "  ".join([f"{name:>6}" for name in class_names])
        print(header)
        print("-" * len(header))
        
        # Print rows
        for i, from_tag in enumerate(class_names):
            row = f"{from_tag:>6}: "
            row += "  ".join([f"{transitions[i, j]:>6.2f}" for j in range(num_tags)])
            print(row)
        
        # Find most likely transitions
        print("\nMost likely transitions:")
        for i in range(num_tags):
            max_j = transitions[i].argmax()
            print(f"  {class_names[i]} -> {class_names[max_j]} (score: {transitions[i, max_j]:.2f})")
        
        if hasattr(crf_layer, 'start_transitions'):
            print("\nStart transition scores:")
            start_trans = crf_layer.start_transitions.detach().cpu().numpy()
            for i, name in enumerate(class_names):
                print(f"  {name}: {start_trans[i]:.2f}")
        
        if hasattr(crf_layer, 'end_transitions'):
            print("\nEnd transition scores:")
            end_trans = crf_layer.end_transitions.detach().cpu().numpy()
            for i, name in enumerate(class_names):
                print(f"  {name}: {end_trans[i]:.2f}")
        
        print("\n")
    
    @staticmethod
    def analyze_predictions(predictions, targets, mask=None):
        """Analyze prediction quality."""
        print("=" * 60)
        print("Prediction Analysis")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        if isinstance(predictions, list):
            # Handle list of predictions (from CRF decode)
            predictions = torch.tensor([p for p in predictions])
        
        if mask is not None:
            # Apply mask
            valid_mask = mask.bool()
            predictions = predictions[valid_mask]
            targets = targets[valid_mask]
        else:
            predictions = predictions.flatten()
            targets = targets.flatten()
        
        # Overall accuracy
        accuracy = (predictions == targets).float().mean().item()
        print(f"\nOverall Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f} ({accuracy*100:.2f}%)")
        
        # Per-class accuracy
        num_classes = targets.max().item() + 1
        print("\nPer-class Accuracy:")
        for c in range(num_classes):
            class_mask = targets == c
            if class_mask.sum() > 0:
                class_acc = (predictions[class_mask] == targets[class_mask]).float().mean().item()
                class_count = class_mask.sum().item()
                print(f"  Class {c}: {class_acc:.4f} ({class_acc*100:.2f}%) - {class_count} samples")
        
        # Confusion statistics
        print("\nMost common errors:")
        confusion_counts = {}
        for pred, true in zip(predictions.tolist(), targets.tolist()):
            if pred != true:
                key = (true, pred)
                confusion_counts[key] = confusion_counts.get(key, 0) + 1
        
        sorted_errors = sorted(confusion_counts.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        for (true_class, pred_class), count in sorted_errors[:5]:
            print(f"  True: {true_class}, Predicted: {pred_class} - {count} times")
        
        print("\n")
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_gradient_flow(model, loss):
        """Check gradient flow through the model."""
        print("=" * 60)
        print("Gradient Flow Analysis")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        print("\nGradient statistics by layer:")
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            if param.grad is not None:
                grad_mean = param.grad.abs().mean().item()
                grad_max = param.grad.abs().max().item()
                grad_min = param.grad.abs().min().item()
                print(f"\n{name}:")
                print(f"  Mean: {grad_mean:.6f}")
                print(f"  Max:  {grad_max:.6f}")
                print(f"  Min:  {grad_min:.6f}")
                
                if grad_mean < 1e-7:
                    print(f"  WARNING: Very small gradients (possible vanishing gradient)")
                elif grad_mean > 1e2:
                    print(f"  WARNING: Very large gradients (possible exploding gradient)")
            else:
                print(f"\n{name}: No gradient")
        
        print("\n")

"""
Advanced Features and Extensions
"""

class HierarchicalStructuredOutput(nn.Module):
    """
    Hierarchical structured output for multi-level predictions.
    Example: Document -> Paragraph -> Sentence -> Token
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        token_dim: int,
        sentence_dim: int,
        paragraph_dim: int,
        num_token_classes: int,
        num_sentence_classes: int
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Token level
        self.token_encoder = nn.LSTM(
            token_dim, 128,
            batch_first=True,
            bidirectional=True
        )
        self.token_crf = CRFLayer(num_token_classes)
        self.token_classifier = nn.Linear(256, num_token_classes)
        
        # Sentence level (aggregates token representations)
        self.sentence_encoder = nn.LSTM(
            256, 128,
            batch_first=True,
            bidirectional=True
        )
        self.sentence_classifier = nn.Linear(256, num_sentence_classes)
        
        # Paragraph level
        self.paragraph_encoder = nn.LSTM(
            256, 128,
            batch_first=True
        )
        self.paragraph_pooling = nn.AdaptiveMaxPool1d(1)
    
    def forward(
        self,
        tokens: torch.Tensor,
        sentence_boundaries: torch.Tensor,
        token_labels: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
    ):
        """
        Args:
            tokens: [batch, max_tokens, token_dim]
            sentence_boundaries: [batch, max_tokens] (1 at sentence end, 0 otherwise)
            token_labels: [batch, max_tokens] (optional, for training)
        """
        batch_size, max_tokens, _ = tokens.shape
        
        # Token-level encoding
        token_features, _ = self.token_encoder(tokens)
        token_emissions = self.token_classifier(token_features)
        
        # Token-level CRF
        if token_labels is not None:
            token_loss = self.token_crf(token_emissions, token_labels)
        else:
            token_loss = None
        
        # Aggregate tokens into sentences
        sentence_features = []
        for b in range(batch_size):
            boundaries = torch.where(sentence_boundaries[b] == 1)[0]
            start = 0
            for end in boundaries:
                # Pool tokens in this sentence
                sent_repr = token_features[b, start:end+1].mean(dim=0)
                sentence_features.append(sent_repr)
                start = end + 1
        
        if sentence_features:
            sentence_features = torch.stack(sentence_features).unsqueeze(0)
            
            # Sentence-level encoding
            sentence_output, _ = self.sentence_encoder(sentence_features)
            sentence_logits = self.sentence_classifier(sentence_output)
        else:
            sentence_logits = None
        
        return token_emissions, sentence_logits, token_loss


class AttentionBasedStructuredOutput(nn.Module):
    """
    Structured output with attention mechanism for capturing long-range dependencies.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        hidden_dim: int,
        num_classes: int,
        num_heads: int = 8,
        num_layers: int = 4
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.input_projection = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        
        # Transformer encoder for capturing dependencies
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=hidden_dim,
            nhead=num_heads,
            dim_feedforward=hidden_dim * 4,
            dropout=0.1,
            batch_first=True
        )
        self.transformer = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers)
        
        # Structured output layer
        self.structured_layer = StructuredPredictionLayer(
            input_dim=hidden_dim,
            num_classes=num_classes,
            hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
            use_attention=True
        )
    
    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        # Project input
        x = self.input_projection(x)
        
        # Apply transformer
        if mask is not None:
            # Create attention mask
            attn_mask = ~mask.bool()
        else:
            attn_mask = None
        
        x = self.transformer(x, src_key_padding_mask=attn_mask)
        
        # Structured prediction
        unary_scores, structured_scores = self.structured_layer(x, mask)
        
        return unary_scores, structured_scores


class NeuralStructuredSVM(nn.Module):
    """
    Neural network with structured SVM loss (max-margin structured prediction).
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        output_dim: int,
        num_classes: int,
        margin: float = 1.0
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.margin = margin
        self.num_classes = num_classes
        
        # Feature encoder
        self.encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, output_dim)
        )
        
        # Scoring function
        self.score_net = nn.Linear(output_dim, num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        features = self.encoder(x)
        scores = self.score_net(features)
        return scores
    
    def structured_hinge_loss(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        y_true: torch.Tensor,
        y_candidates: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute structured hinge loss.
        
        Args:
            x: Input [batch_size, seq_len, input_dim]
            y_true: True labels [batch_size, seq_len]
            y_candidates: Candidate structures [batch_size, num_candidates, seq_len]
        """
        batch_size, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        
        # Compute scores for true structure
        scores = self.forward(x)  # [batch, seq_len, num_classes]
        
        true_scores = scores.gather(
            2, y_true.unsqueeze(2)
        ).squeeze(2).sum(dim=1)  # [batch]
        
        # Compute scores for candidate structures
        num_candidates = y_candidates.shape[1]
        max_violation = torch.zeros(batch_size, device=x.device)
        
        for c in range(num_candidates):
            y_cand = y_candidates[:, c, :]  # [batch, seq_len]
            
            # Hamming distance (loss augmentation)
            hamming_dist = (y_cand != y_true).float().sum(dim=1)
            
            # Candidate scores
            cand_scores = scores.gather(
                2, y_cand.unsqueeze(2)
            ).squeeze(2).sum(dim=1)
            
            # Margin violation
            violation = cand_scores + hamming_dist - true_scores
            max_violation = torch.maximum(max_violation, violation)
        
        # Hinge loss
        loss = torch.clamp(max_violation, min=0).mean()
        
        return loss


class BeamSearchDecoder:
    """
    Beam search decoder for structured output.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, beam_size: int = 5):
        self.beam_size = beam_size
    
    def decode(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        max_length: int,
        num_classes: int
    ) -> List[Tuple[List[int], float]]:
        """
        Perform beam search decoding.
        
        Args:
            model: Model that outputs scores
            x: Input tensor
            max_length: Maximum sequence length
            num_classes: Number of classes
            
        Returns:
            List of (sequence, score) tuples
        """
        batch_size = x.shape[0]
        device = x.device
        
        # Initialize beams
        beams = [([], 0.0)]  # (sequence, cumulative_score)
        
        for t in range(max_length):
            candidates = []
            
            for seq, score in beams:
                # Get current context
                if len(seq) == 0:
                    context = x
                else:
                    # This is simplified; actual implementation depends on model
                    context = x
                
                # Get scores for next token (simplified)
                with torch.no_grad():
                    next_scores = model(context)
                    if next_scores.dim() == 3:
                        next_scores = next_scores[:, t, :]
                    next_scores = torch.log_softmax(next_scores, dim=-1)
                
                # Expand beam
                for c in range(num_classes):
                    new_seq = seq + [c]
                    new_score = score + next_scores[0, c].item()
                    candidates.append((new_seq, new_score))
            
            # Keep top-k candidates
            candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
            beams = candidates[:self.beam_size]
        
        return beams

"""
Best Practices and Tips
"""
def print_best_practices():
    """Print best practices for structured output models."""
    print("=" * 80)
    print(" BEST PRACTICES FOR STRUCTURED OUTPUT MODELS ".center(80, "="))
    print("=" * 80)
    
    practices = """
1. CHOOSING THE RIGHT MODEL:
   - CRF: Sequential data with strong Markov dependencies (NER, POS tagging)
   - MRF: Spatial data with local dependencies (image segmentation)
   - Graphical Models: Arbitrary graph structures (molecules, social networks)
   - Energy-Based: When you can define a good energy function
   - Structured Prediction: When you need flexible dependency modeling

2. DATA PREPROCESSING:
   - Handle variable-length sequences with padding and masking
   - Normalize features for stable training
   - Use appropriate data augmentation for your domain

3. TRAINING TIPS:
   - Start with smaller models and gradually increase complexity
   - Use gradient clipping (typically 5.0) to prevent exploding gradients
   - Monitor both structured and unstructured metrics
   - Use learning rate scheduling (ReduceLROnPlateau works well
```python
   - Use learning rate scheduling (ReduceLROnPlateau works well)
   - Consider warmup for complex models
   - Use dropout (0.3-0.5) to prevent overfitting

4. INFERENCE OPTIMIZATION:
   - Cache computations when possible
   - Use beam search for better quality (slower)
   - Use greedy/Viterbi for speed (faster)
   - Batch inference when possible
   - Consider approximate inference for large graphs

5. DEBUGGING:
   - Visualize learned transition matrices (for CRF)
   - Check gradient flow through all layers
   - Validate on simple synthetic data first
   - Monitor per-class performance
   - Track transition patterns in predictions

6. HYPERPARAMETER TUNING:
   - Hidden dimensions: Start with 128-256
   - Number of layers: 2-4 for most tasks
   - Learning rate: 0.001 for Adam is a good starting point
   - Batch size: 16-32 for sequences, larger for images
   - Number of message passing iterations: 3-5 for graphical models

7. COMMON PITFALLS:
   - Forgetting to apply masks for variable-length sequences
   - Not normalizing pairwise potentials
   - Overfitting on small datasets (use regularization)
   - Ignoring class imbalance
   - Not validating on held-out data

8. PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION:
   - Use mixed precision training (torch.cuda.amp)
   - Profile code to find bottlenecks
   - Vectorize operations instead of loops
   - Use efficient data loading (num_workers > 0)
   - Consider model distillation for deployment

9. MODEL SELECTION:
   - Use cross-validation for small datasets
   - Track multiple metrics (accuracy, F1, etc.)
   - Consider computational budget for deployment
   - Test on domain-specific edge cases

10. PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT:
    - Convert to TorchScript or ONNX for faster inference
    - Implement proper error handling
    - Monitor prediction confidence
    - Log predictions for analysis
    - Version control your models
    """
    
    print(practices)
    print("\n" + "=" * 80 + "\n")


"""
Comprehensive Testing Suite
"""
class StructuredOutputTestSuite:
    """Comprehensive test suite for structured output models."""
    
    @staticmethod
    def test_model_forward_backward(model, sample_input, sample_target):
        """Test forward and backward pass."""
        print("Testing forward/backward pass...")
        
        try:
            # Forward pass
            if isinstance(sample_input, tuple):
                output = model(*sample_input)
            else:
                output = model(sample_input)
            
            # Compute loss
            if isinstance(output, tuple):
                loss = output[0] if output[0].dim() == 0 else output[0].mean()
            else:
                loss = F.cross_entropy(
                    output.reshape(-1, output.shape[-1]),
                    sample_target.reshape(-1)
                )
            
            # Backward pass
            loss.backward()
            
            print(f"  ✓ Forward/backward pass successful")
            print(f"  Loss: {loss.item():.4f}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  ✗ Error: {str(e)}")
            return False
    
    @staticmethod
    def test_model_inference(model, sample_input):
        """Test inference mode."""
        print("Testing inference mode...")
        
        try:
            model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                if isinstance(sample_input, tuple):
                    output = model(*sample_input)
                else:
                    output = model(sample_input)
            
            print(f"  ✓ Inference successful")
            if isinstance(output, torch.Tensor):
                print(f"  Output shape: {output.shape}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  ✗ Error: {str(e)}")
            return False
    
    @staticmethod
    def test_gradient_flow(model, sample_input, sample_target):
        """Test that gradients flow through all parameters."""
        print("Testing gradient flow...")
        
        try:
            model.zero_grad()
            
            # Forward and backward
            if isinstance(sample_input, tuple):
                output = model(*sample_input)
            else:
                output = model(sample_input)
            
            if isinstance(output, tuple):
                loss = output[0] if output[0].dim() == 0 else output[0].mean()
            else:
                loss = F.cross_entropy(
                    output.reshape(-1, output.shape[-1]),
                    sample_target.reshape(-1)
                )
            
            loss.backward()
            
            # Check gradients
            params_with_grad = 0
            params_without_grad = 0
            
            for name, param in model.named_parameters():
                if param.requires_grad:
                    if param.grad is not None and param.grad.abs().sum() > 0:
                        params_with_grad += 1
                    else:
                        params_without_grad += 1
                        print(f"  Warning: No gradient for {name}")
            
            print(f"  ✓ Parameters with gradients: {params_with_grad}")
            if params_without_grad > 0:
                print(f"  ⚠ Parameters without gradients: {params_without_grad}")
            
            return params_without_grad == 0
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  ✗ Error: {str(e)}")
            return False
    
    @staticmethod
    def test_overfitting_single_batch(model, sample_input, sample_target, num_steps=100):
        """Test if model can overfit a single batch (sanity check)."""
        print("Testing overfitting on single batch...")
        
        try:
            model.train()
            optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
            
            initial_loss = None
            final_loss = None
            
            for step in range(num_steps):
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                
                if isinstance(sample_input, tuple):
                    output = model(*sample_input)
                else:
                    output = model(sample_input)
                
                if isinstance(output, tuple):
                    loss = output[0] if output[0].dim() == 0 else output[0].mean()
                else:
                    loss = F.cross_entropy(
                        output.reshape(-1, output.shape[-1]),
                        sample_target.reshape(-1)
                    )
                
                if step == 0:
                    initial_loss = loss.item()
                
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                
                if step == num_steps - 1:
                    final_loss = loss.item()
            
            improvement = initial_loss - final_loss
            print(f"  Initial loss: {initial_loss:.4f}")
            print(f"  Final loss: {final_loss:.4f}")
            print(f"  Improvement: {improvement:.4f}")
            
            if improvement > 0:
                print(f"  ✓ Model can learn (loss decreased)")
                return True
            else:
                print(f"  ✗ Model not learning (loss did not decrease)")
                return False
        except Exception as e:

    @staticmethod

        return results

    @staticmethod
    def benchmark_inference_speed(model, sample_input, num_iterations=100):
        """Benchmark inference speed."""
        import time
        
        print("Benchmarking inference speed...")
        model.eval()
        
        # Warmup
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(10):
                if isinstance(sample_input, tuple):
                    _ = model(*sample_input)
                else:
                    _ = model(sample_input)
        
        # Benchmark
        start_time = time.time()
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(num_iterations):
                if isinstance(sample_input, tuple):
                    _ = model(*sample_input)
                else:
                    _ = model(sample_input)
        end_time = time.time()
        
        avg_time = (end_time - start_time) / num_iterations
        throughput = 1.0 / avg_time
        
        print(f"  Average inference time: {avg_time*1000:.2f} ms")
        print(f"  Throughput: {throughput:.2f} samples/sec")
        
        return avg_time, throughput
    
    @staticmethod
    def benchmark_memory_usage(model, sample_input):
        """Benchmark memory usage."""
        print("Benchmarking memory usage...")
        
        # Count parameters
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
        trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
        
        # Estimate memory (rough)
        param_memory_mb = total_params * 4 / (1024 ** 2)  # Assuming float32
        
        print(f"  Total parameters: {total_params:,}")
        print(f"  Trainable parameters: {trainable_params:,}")
        print(f"  Estimated parameter memory: {param_memory_mb:.2f} MB")
        
        return total_params, param_memory_mb
